title: monado-viture: Luma Ultra as a Monado OpenXR device on sfub
description:
# monado-viture: the Luma Ultra as a Monado OpenXR device on sfub

Goal: a working OpenXR path for the VITURE Luma Ultra on Linux through an
out-of-tree `xrt_device` driver in Monado, so the glasses are an HMD surface
rather than a phone-only accessory. sfub drives it; the Fold5 thin-client path
and UxSpace are untouched.

- driver + docs + scripts: `experiments/monado-viture/`
- Monado checkout: `/home/sf/workspace/monado` (patch APPLIED, base `e936b6a`)
- runtime shape: out-of-process. `scripts/build` -> `scripts/run-service` (the
  service owns the unix socket) -> `scripts/run-hello-xr`
- headless validation uses the compute compositor (`XRT_COMPOSITOR_COMPUTE=1`)

## milestones (measured 2026-09-28/29, commits 1a04a9e..dbc60b4)

| | milestone | state | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| M0 | build Monado on sfub without root | DONE | exit 0, zero warnings, patch APPLIED vs `e936b6a` |
| M1 | static VITURE HMD instantiates via OpenXR | DONE | `Head: 'VITURE (pid 0x0000)'`, 2 views, panel 3840x1200@90 sbs |
| M1 | hello_xr runs stereo against it | DONE | both swapchains 2688x1680, `XR_SESSION_STATE_FOCUSED`, 0 errors, exit 0 |
| M2 | stereo actually reaches the panels | blocked | hardware gate |
| M3 | Carina 3DoF rotation drives HMD orientation | blocked | hardware gate |
| M4 | BeamNG native Linux OpenXR starts and tracks | not started | `scripts/run-beamng` refuses until M0-M3 are measured |
| M5 | Carina 6DoF translation | not started | 6DoF is the default path, unit unverified |
| M6 | recentering, prediction, latency tuning | not started | |

## blocking gate

The Luma is not attached to sfub, and the seat user cannot open its USB devnode
until the root-owned udev rule is in place:

    sudo cp experiments/monado-viture/udev/70-viture-xr.rules /etc/udev/rules.d/
    sudo udevadm control --reload && sudo udevadm trigger

M2 and M3 carry `blocks` dependencies on the gate bead, so `br ready` stays
honest while the glass is off the desk.

## operational hazards found while measuring M0/M1

- **stale IPC socket.** A killed `monado-service` leaves
  `/run/user/1000/monado_comp_ipc`; the next start dies with `Address already in
  use`. `scripts/run-service` now clears a socket that no live process owns.
- **X connector-metadata flap.** After Vulkan/DRM work X reported
  `DP-0 disconnected ... 0mm x 0mm` (once a transient `3440/910x1440/381` where
  the EDID says `797x333`) while the kernel still reported `card1-DP-1 connected`
  with a valid EDID. Mode, refresh, layout, primary flag and 110x110 dpi were all
  unaffected -- only X's per-output metadata went stale. Cause unestablished;
  expect it again at M2.

## out of scope

Recentering/prediction/latency tuning (M6), any Android-side integration, and
anything that changes UxSpace or the Fold thin client. Failed or blocked work
stays open; the epic closes on operator acceptance of M2/M3.
acceptance_criteria: M2 and M3 measured on sfub with the glasses attached, and the operator accepts the result.

title: Recon: XR invariants, local display/GPU stack, Monado driver model, VITURE SDK, prior art
description:
Read the XR workspace rules, then establish the substrate before writing code:

- local: X11/NVIDIA/glasses/DRM/Vulkan state, including the pre-existing phantom
  1920x1200@90 HDMI-0 output
- Monado: how an out-of-tree `xrt_device` is registered and built (`XRT_BUILD_DRIVER_*`)
- VITURE: which Linux SDK pieces exist for Carina/pose, and what the native libs need
- prior art: Breezy / xr_driver / Monado branches touching VITURE

Findings landed in `experiments/monado-viture/docs/`.
acceptance_criteria: The build path, the driver insertion point and the SDK's Linux surface are known and written down; no unresolved how-would-this-attach question remains.
close_reason: recon complete; findings recorded in experiments/monado-viture/docs/

title: Scaffold experiments/monado-viture: driver tree, build, display safety
description:
Create the experiment tree and the safety rails:

- `src/` driver sources, plus `docs/`, `scripts/`, `tools/`, `udev/`
- `scripts/patch-monado.sh` (idempotent patch against a recorded base)
- `scripts/install-deps-local.sh` (private sysroot, no root)
- `scripts/restore-display` and a real topology snapshot before touching displays

This workstation's X topology has to survive every experiment, so restoring it
must be a two-command operation rather than an adventure.
acceptance_criteria: Tree exists; patch/install/build/restore scripts run; a topology snapshot is on disk before any display-affecting step.
close_reason: scaffold landed; snapshot taken, restore validated read-only

title: M0: build Monado on sfub (patched, private sysroot, no root)
description:
Patch a clean Monado checkout to register the VITURE driver, then build it
against a private sysroot -- no root, no system package changes.

`scripts/build` owns the whole path: patch -> configure -> ninja -> report.
Verified: exit 0, `ninja: no work to do` on re-run, zero warnings, both runtime
artifacts emitted (service binary + driver .so).
acceptance_criteria: `scripts/build` exits 0 with the patch applied and both artifacts present, with no root and no system-wide install.
close_reason: M0 measured: build exit 0, zero warnings, patch APPLIED vs e936b6a

title: M1: static VITURE HMD instantiates via OpenXR and hello_xr runs stereo
description:
With no vendor SDK and no hardware attached, the driver must still create a
usable HMD (`VITURE_NO_SDK=1`: static HMD, no tracking, panel 3840x1200@90 sbs,
2 views).

Then drive a real OpenXR client against the out-of-process service end-to-end:

    scripts/run-service
    scripts/run-hello-xr -g Vulkan --space Local

Verified: `Head: 'VITURE (pid 0x0000)'`, OrientationTracking + PositionTracking
reported, both swapchains 2688x1680, `XR_SESSION_STATE_FOCUSED`, 0 errors, exit 0.
acceptance_criteria: hello_xr reaches XR_SESSION_STATE_FOCUSED against the built runtime with two 2688x1680 swapchains and zero errors.
close_reason: M1 measured on the committed build path: FOCUSED, both swapchains 2688x1680, 0 errors, exit 0

title: Bug: run entry points were broken (4 defects) + add scripts/run-service
description:
Found by re-reading the committed scripts instead of trusting them:

- `run-hello-xr` pointed at a non-existent `hello_xr` path (OpenXR-SDK builds it
  under `build/src/tests/`), omitted the loader dir from `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, and
  consumed its first positional as a binary path -- so the documented
  `run-hello-xr -g Vulkan` searched for a program literally named `-g`
- `scripts/build` summary `find` had an `-o` / `-maxdepth` precedence bug
- the `run-beamng` gate text claimed M0/M1 were unvalidated
- `restore-display` had no snapshot to restore to, so `restore` would have died

Plus `scripts/run-service`, because a killed service leaves
`/run/user/1000/monado_comp_ipc` and the next start dies with `Address already in
use` -- hit twice in one session.
acceptance_criteria: Every documented entry point runs end-to-end through the documented invocation, and a stale socket no longer blocks a restart.
close_reason: entry points fixed and re-verified end-to-end; wrapper proven on the real stale-socket case

title: Docs: architecture, coordinates, measurements
description:
Write down what the driver actually is while it is still fresh:

- `docs/architecture.md`: processes, socket, registry/plugin layout, compute vs display compositor
- `docs/coordinates.md`: pose / axis conventions and the verification procedure
- `docs/measurements.md`: M0/M1 evidence, hashes, and the exact commands used

Declared domain: the OpenXR/Linux driver experiment. The Fold5 thin-client path
and UxSpace are separate and must not leak into these docs.
acceptance_criteria: Architecture, coordinate conventions and the M0/M1 measurement record are in the repo and match observed behavior.
close_reason: docs written and cross-referenced from the experiment README

title: Hardware gate: attach the Luma Ultra to sfub and install the udev rule
description:
**Human action -- do not claim.**

The Luma Ultra is not attached to sfub, and the seat user cannot open its USB
devnode until the root-owned udev rule exists. M2 and M3 both block on this.

    sudo cp experiments/monado-viture/udev/70-viture-xr.rules /etc/udev/rules.d/
    sudo udevadm control --reload && sudo udevadm trigger

then attach the glasses. Closing this bead asserts the rule is installed *and*
the device opened from the seat user's own session, with no root and no sudo
wrapper.
acceptance_criteria: Seat user opens the VITURE device on sfub after the udev rule is installed, without sudo.

title: M2: stereo reaches the Luma panels
description:
Once the glass is attached, get real per-eye output onto the panels instead of
the compute compositor's offscreen path:

1. `tools/viture-pose-dump --seconds 10 --json` -- confirm the device opens and streams
2. start the service on the vendor path (`VITURE_NO_SDK=0`) and run
   `scripts/run-hello-xr` with the display compositor
3. confirm distinct per-eye content and that 3840x1200 sbs actually scans out

Record the xrandr/DP state before and after: if X re-probes the connector, that
belongs in the epic's hazard list, not in silence.
acceptance_criteria: Both eyes show the expected distinct stereo content driven by hello_xr, and the workstation display topology is unchanged afterwards.

title: M3: Carina 3DoF rotation drives HMD orientation
description:
Feed the Carina pose stream into HMD orientation and prove the axes are right,
not merely present:

1. characterise the stream: `tools/viture-pose-dump --seconds 10 --json`
2. `scripts/test-coordinates` (offline axis / yaw-pitch-roll units) must pass
3. drive rotation and watch the HMD orientation respond with the correct sign and
   axis -- no inversion, no swapped axes

The axes procedure in `docs/coordinates.md` is the acceptance protocol.
acceptance_criteria: Yaw/pitch/roll from the glasses reproduce in the HMD pose with correct signs and axes, per the documented procedure.

title: console recorder v1: reliable Luma RGB + selectable audio field capture
description: Existing recorder scaffold already provides foreground service, segmented MediaMuxer recording, VITURE RGB integration, default-route audio, metadata/events, and automated smoke tooling. This campaign empirically verifies the attached Luma hardware; adds semantic microphone enumeration, persistence, explicit routing, requested-vs-actual provenance, and hotplug handling; verifies RGB/video, audio, muxing, segmentation, lifecycle, and 30s+ smoke; characterizes any Android-exposed Luma microphone; supports Bluetooth inputs with physical-device validation left open when absent; records sunlight cursor findings; and updates docs to measured state. Current baseline attempt on 2026-09-29 found the Fold SSH transport unreachable (No route to host) despite glasses reported attached, so hardware work resumes immediately when transport returns.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Real Luma front RGB frames recorded on Fold. 2. Selectable Android input devices implemented and actual route verified. 3. Valid synchronized video plus selected-mic audio in MP4. 4. Foreground/background behavior mechanically verified. 5. Segmentation and metadata mechanically verified. 6. 30s+ automated hardware smoke passes. 7. Metadata records selection mode and requested/actual mic. 8. Available glasses mic characterized if Android exposes it. 9. Bluetooth path supported and tested when suitable device available. 10. Sunlight cursor findings/workaround recorded. 11. Docs describe measured state. Epic remains open until field-usable; unavailable physical Bluetooth validation remains an explicit open gate.

title: audit recorder and establish measured hardware baseline
description: Review current implementation without rewriting it, build HEAD, deploy through xrctl, enumerate app/adb audio inputs, and run the existing attached-Luma smoke path. Record transport or hardware blockers as measured facts.
acceptance_criteria: Current source and runtime baseline documented with build, device, audio enumeration, and smoke evidence; failures classified mechanically.

Do not route by product-name literals.

title: verify and fix Luma RGB capture and encoding
description: With connected Luma, prove native front RGB open, frame arrival, dimensions/fps, codec, drops, and encode stability. Measure the existing MJPEG-Bitmap-ARGB-YUV path before optimizing.
acceptance_criteria: Real Luma RGB produces a playable MP4 video track with measured codec, resolution, fps, drops, CPU/thermal observations, and no fatal crash.

title: verify muxing timestamps segmentation and provenance metadata
description: Verify synchronized AAC/video muxing, monotonic timestamps, reduced-duration rollover, independent segment playback, stats, and audio selection/requested/actual metadata plus route events.
acceptance_criteria: Two short rolled segments parse and play independently; timestamps/duration sane; session/events metadata parses and accurately records routes and stats.

comments.author: sf
comments.text: Smoke now pulls every MP4 segment and requires at least two independently ffprobeable segments, each with video and audio tracks. Stop ordering was fixed so both encoders drain before MediaMuxer closes. Runtime timestamp/rollover acceptance remains blocked by Fold transport.

title: verify foreground lifecycle disconnect and error behavior
description: Mechanically exercise activity background, foreground service survival, stop finalization, selected input removal where possible, and fatal/low-level error cleanup without corrupt sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Service records while activity is backgrounded, stop finalizes output, and tested disconnect/error paths stop explicitly with parseable session evidence.

comments.author: sf
comments.text: Code review found stop ordering risk: audio was stopped before encode thread, allowing video output to target a muxer after audio EOS and during shutdown. Changed stop order to join video encode, then stop/drain audio, then close muxer. Build passes; runtime lifecycle verification remains blocked by Fold transport.

description: Extend existing smoke tooling only where needed to check 30s+ Luma source, requested/actual mic, non-silent audio RMS/peak, tracks, codec/fps/resolution/bitrate/storage, metadata, crashes, and service health.
acceptance_criteria: A >=30s automated attached-hardware run pulls and inspects its sample and reports all required video/audio/provenance/health metrics.

title: validate connected Bluetooth microphone routing
description: Physical validation gate. When an appropriate Bluetooth input is attached and Android enumerates it, select it, verify actual routed device, record non-silent audio, and inspect the final AAC track. Do not claim DJI-specific validation without a DJI device.
acceptance_criteria: A connected Bluetooth input is empirically enumerated, selected, routed, recorded, and verified non-silent; exact device/type recorded. Remains open when hardware is absent.
